extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians specializing in arithmetic geometry/Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted constraints, structural requirements, and conceptual conditions needed for the logical structure and constructions in Inter‑Universal Teichmüller Theory (IUT); these are the formal/semantic conditions the exposition requires for its arguments to operate. Targeted at researchers working on/reading IUT.

rubrics_metrics.name: Synchronization of Iord ±-indeterminacies relative to F_l-symmetry and valuations
rubrics_metrics.description: the Iord ±-indeterminacies of (iv-a) may be synchronized relative to the F_l-symmetry by applying the “linear disjointness” of the theory of κ-coric functions from SL2(Fl); and relative to the distinct valuations v ∈ V in local-global comparisons of the Kummer theories/Galois evaluation operations of (i-c) by means of comparison with the cyclotomic rigidity isomorphisms arising from the Kummer theories of (i-a) — but not relative to the domain/codomain of the log-link since the relevant [Frobenius-like] monoids in the domain/codomain of the log-link are not set-theoretically related to one another via the log-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains where synchronization is possible (via F_l-symmetry and valuation comparisons) and where it fails (not via log-link); references [Alien], §3.6 and IUTch remarks for justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: F_l-symmetricity of the Kummer theory/Galois evaluation of (i-c)
rubrics_metrics.description: the F_l-symmetricity of the Kummer theory/Galois evaluation of (i-c) underlies the compatibility and synchronization properties of (iv-c), (iv-e).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This symmetricity is cited as a fundamental aspect enabling later compatibilities; see IUTchII/IUTchIII remarks cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualitative difference when F_3±-symmetricity fails (behavior of (i-b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Kummer theory/Galois evaluation of (i-b), which does not satisfy the condition of F_3±-symmetricity, exhibits qualitatively fundamentally different behavior from the F_l-symmetric Kummer theory/Galois evaluation of (i-c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Points to incompatibility issues when attempting to apply techniques suited to F_l-symmetric situations to F_3±-asymmetric situations; see discussion of (v) and references.

rubrics_metrics.name: SimCon: a priori self-contradictory trivial/nontrivial action condition under F_3±-symmetry
rubrics_metrics.description: In attempts to compare via the F_3±-symmetry the Kummer theories/Galois evaluation operations at different t ∈ F_l one may be forced into a self-contradictory situation in which the F_3±-symmetry permutes the labels “t ∈ F_l” nontrivially but acts trivially on the (non-F_3±-symmetric) étale theta function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ‘SimCon’ situation is identified as an obstruction; resolving it requires working with invariants (see (v-e)) or changing the Kummer-theoretic framework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Étale theta function as cohomology class with asymmetric F_3± action
rubrics_metrics.description: In the context of Galois evaluation, the étale theta function may be thought of as a cohomology class ∈ H^1(some closed subgroup of Π_v, some cyclotome associated to the Galois evaluation label t ∈ F_l) where the F_3±-symmetry acts nontrivially on the Galois evaluation cyclotome (the second argument of H^1(−)) but trivially on the closed subgroup of Π_v (the first argument).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes the mismatched action of symmetry on the two slots of H^1, explaining why SimCon arises and why invariance considerations matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Profinite Kummer-theory pathology under N-th power replacement of theta functions
rubrics_metrics.description: A profinite Kummer theory situation of this sort occurs if one replaces the theta functions in IUT by their N-th powers (N ≥ 2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives an example of how naively modifying theta functions leads to the problematic profinite situation; see IUTchIII remarks referenced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resolution by invariants / single unified set-theoretic basepoint
rubrics_metrics.description: The only ‘solution’ to the SimCon simultaneous trivial/nontrivial action condition is to work with objects invariant with respect to the F_3±-symmetry — concretely, with a single unified set-theoretic basepoint which allows computation of F_3±-symmetrizing isomorphisms by projecting to a single copy of G_v determined by that basepoint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposes invariants/basepoint as the mechanism to resolve contradictory action conditions; cross-references Example 3.8.3 and related remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid conjugacy indeterminacies that make cyclotomes ill-defined up to Z×-multiples
rubrics_metrics.description: Conjugacy indeterminacies inherent in profinite Kummer-theory F_3±-symmetrizing isomorphisms make any single unified basepoint well-defined only up to conjugacy, which is unacceptable as it would render coefficient cyclotomes and étale theta functions defined only up to Z×-multiples (i.e., theta values only up to Z×-powers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: States why conjugacy indeterminacies are pathological for IUT constructions and motivates the need for a different framework (truncation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Replace profinite Kummer theory by truncated Kummer theory to avoid pathologies
rubrics_metrics.description: To avoid the pathologies of conjugacy indeterminacies one must replace the profinite Kummer theory by the truncated Kummer theory of (i-b), so that one can apply a single unified basepoint that is well-defined up to geometric fundamental group conjugacy (which does not affect the computation of F_3±-symmetrizing isomorphisms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is presented as the acceptable method to obtain a basepoint well-defined up to harmless indeterminacies; references to [Alien], §3.6 and IUTchII remarks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Truncatibility of the Kummer theory/Galois evaluation of (i-b) is fundamental
rubrics_metrics.description: The truncatibility of the Kummer theory/Galois evaluation operations of (i-b) plays a fundamental role in the logical structure of IUT.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary statement justifying the previous items: truncation is essential to avoid profinite pathologies and to enable the theory's logical structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single unified basepoint determined by connected subgraph Γ^3 ⊆ Γ
rubrics_metrics.description: The single unified basepoint is completely determined by the connected subgraph Γ^3_X ⊆ Γ_X (equivalently Γ^3 ⊆ Γ^¨Y); this subgraph may be thought of as a ‘copy Γ of the real line R’ with integers as vertices and segments as edges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduces the combinatorial/dynamical object (Γ^3) that fixes the basepoint; references IUTchII remarks for uniqueness conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent action of geometric fundamental groups on vertices (vi-a)
rubrics_metrics.description: The various geometric fundamental groups ‘Δ’ that appear act on the various vertices t ∈ {−l_2, …, −1, 0, 1, …, l_2} ⊆ Γ independently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirement on how Δ acts on Γ-vertices; used to track indeterminacies and orbit structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action of Δ corresponds to G_Γ = <l·Z, ±1> (vi-b)
rubrics_metrics.description: The actions of geometric fundamental groups Δ on the copy Γ of R amount to the conventional action of the group generated by translations by elements of l·Z and multiplication by −1 on R (notation: G_Γ := l·Z ⋊ {±1}).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the concrete group structure governing translations and sign-change symmetries acting on Γ.

rubrics_metrics.name: 0 must be a vertex in Γ^3_Z for crucial theta-splittings (vi-c)
rubrics_metrics.description: Since vertex 0 ∈ Γ is the unique vertex used to define the crucial splittings of theta monoids, it is necessary that 0 ∈ Γ^3_Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A necessary combinatorial/normalization condition to allow key splittings; cited from IUTchII Corollary 2.6 (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: G_Γ-indeterminacy if Γ^3 contains components not in l·Z (vi-d)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Γ^3 contains a connected component not contained in l·Z (⊆ Γ) then any theta value q_j^2_v obtained via Galois evaluation for j in that component ∩ Z is well-defined only up to a G_Γ-indeterminacy (possible confusion between j and G_Γ-translates j').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies when theta-values become ambiguous due to orbit translations; motivates containment in l·Z.

rubrics_metrics.name: Theta values for j ∈ Γ^3_Z are well-defined only up to G_Γ-indeterminacy inside Γ^3_Z (vi-e)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any theta value obtained via Galois evaluation for j ∈ Γ^3_Z is well-defined only up to a G_Γ-indeterminacy within Γ^3_Z, i.e., confusion between j and G_Γ-translates inside Γ^3_Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refines the previous point to the case j in Γ^3_Z; stresses the limited extent of acceptable indeterminacy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid indeterminacies that would violate the global product formula (vi-f)
rubrics_metrics.description: Indeterminacies concerning j, j' for nonzero j,j' ∈ Z with distinct absolute values would result in indeterminacies in the ‘vector of ratios’ that determines realiﬁed Gaussian Frobenioids and would violate the global product formula relating value groups at different v ∈ V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A global arithmetic constraint: certain orbit/label confusions are forbidden because they would break fundamental product relations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity of ±Γ^3_Z/{±1} → Z/G_Γ (vi-g)
rubrics_metrics.description: The natural map from the set of {±1}-orbits of ±Γ^3_Z to the set of G_Γ-orbits in Z is injective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A combinatorial injectivity requirement ensuring distinctness of classes under the relevant symmetries; cited to IUTchII Remark 2.6.3 (ii).

rubrics_metrics.name: Connectedness of the subgraph Γ^3 ⊆ Γ (vi-h)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subgraph Γ^3 ⊆ Γ is connected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topological/combinatorial condition necessary for the single unified basepoint construction; referenced in IUTchII.

rubrics_metrics.name: Containment and normalization of Γ^3: 0 ∈ Γ^3 and Γ^3 ⊆ [−l_2, l_2] (vi-i)
rubrics_metrics.description: Γ^3 ⊆ Γ is a connected subgraph that contains 0 and is contained in the closed interval [−l_2, l_2].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Combines earlier conditions to give a bounded connected subgraph normalization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetry assumption Γ^3_Z = ±Γ^3_Z may be assumed without loss (vi-j)
rubrics_metrics.description: Replacing Γ^3_Z by ±Γ^3_Z does not affect validity of (vi-i) or how Γ^3_Z is used in IUT; thus one may assume the symmetry condition Γ^3_Z = ±Γ^3_Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows working under a symmetry hypothesis to simplify combinatorial choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optimization condition maximizing average of squares j^2 (vi-k)
rubrics_metrics.description: Estimates in IUT are optimized precisely when the average of the squares j^2 of the nonzero elements j ∈ Γ^3_Z is maximized, i.e., when Γ^3 = ±Γ^3_Z equals the closed interval [−l_2, l_2] (making the natural map of (vi-g) bijective).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An optimization principle used to uniquely determine Γ^3 under stated symmetry and injectivity conditions; references to IUTchIII/IUTchIV results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treat topological groups as abstract topological groups (not as Galois groups requiring ring/scheme data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Topological groups that arise (often as Galois groups or arithmetic fundamental groups) must be treated as abstract topological groups rather than as Galois groups or arithmetic fundamental groups, because treating them as the latter would require ring/scheme structures not common across the log/Θ-link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This methodological requirement motivates use of anabelian results and weaker coric structures; see discussion at §3.2 and related references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permit and manage richer indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3) and work up to suitable indeterminacies (ExtInd2)
rubrics_metrics.description: IUT must allow for various indeterminacies (Ind1, Ind2, Ind3) more involved than simple inner automorphisms; one must consent to work with objects ‘up to certain suitable indeterminacies’ (e.g., via poly-morphisms) and identify objects via collections of isomorphisms uniquely determined up to these indeterminacies using (ExtInd2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains why many ∨-relations appear and how (ExtInd2) provides identification mechanisms analogous to classical universal constructions (algebraic closures, limits, homology).

rubrics_metrics.name: Regard many outputs stack-theoretically; only pass to set-theoretic quotient at final closed loop (LVsQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Output data of functorial algorithms is often regarded ‘stack-theoretically’ (a collection of set-theoretic objects linked by poly-isomorphisms) rather than as a single set-theoretic object; one arrives at a set-theoretic situation only after obtaining a formal (sub)quotient that forms a ‘closed loop’, at which point one may pass to a coarse/set-theoretic (sub)quotient by taking the log-volume.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the categorical/stacky nature of outputs and the final step required to obtain concrete set-theoretic objects; references [Alien] and IUTchIII steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two viewpoints for treating output data: UdOut vs InOut (descent dichotomy)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applying functorial algorithms there are two treatments of output data: (UdOut) consider output independently as an ‘underlying structure’; or (InOut) consider output together with the input data and algorithm used to construct it. The notation uses suffixes (Π_v) or omission to indicate InOut vs UdOut.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sets a convention for how to regard outputs and how that is reflected notationally (sQGOut, MnOut, PSOut examples illustrate conventions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Descent criterion for functorial algorithms (existence of functorial isomorphism)
rubrics_metrics.description: A functorial algorithm Φ in the original data descends to a functorial algorithm Ψ in the underlying data iff there exists a functorial isomorphism Φ → Ψ|original_data between Φ and the restriction of Ψ.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the formal meaning of ‘descent’ in this context; used to show many constructions do not depend on finer input data up to unique isomorphism.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cohomology and other constructions descend to underlying objects (HmDsc example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Constructions of (co)homology modules, which a priori require a resolution, typically descend (up to unique isomorphism) to constructions whose input data is solely the given module.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A standard illustrative example of descent emphasizing that concrete outputs often depend only on coarse input.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topological multiplicative monoid construction descends to G_k (MnDsc)
rubrics_metrics.description: The topological multiplicative monoid determined by the topological ring [union with {0} of] O(Π_X) — a priori functorial in Π_X — in fact descends, relative to passage to the underlying quotient group, to a functorial algorithm in the topological group G_k.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A central example specific to IUT showing how monoid constructions descend from Π_X to G_k; references Alien §2.12 and AbsTopIII results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiradial/log-Kummer-correspondence/Galois evaluation exhibits Θ-pilot as one possibility in a stack-theoretic family
rubrics_metrics.description: The multiradial algorithm, and especially its log-Kummer-correspondence and Galois-evaluation portion, exhibits the Frobenius-like Θ-pilot as one possibility within a collection of possibilities constructed via anabelian algorithms from étale-like data — not as a single set element but as one possibility up to isomorphism within a possibly non-set-theoretic collection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains how the Θ-pilot is obtained within a stacky family and why log-volume/closed-loop steps are needed to get a set-theoretic object.

rubrics_metrics.name: Logical-correspondence: AND ↔ simultaneous execution/gluing; OR ↔ indeterminacies/poly-morphisms/(sub)quotients
rubrics_metrics.description: Logical AND ‘∧’ corresponds to simultaneous execution and gluing; logical OR ‘∨’ corresponds to indeterminacies, poly-morphisms, and projection/(sub)quotient/splitting. The essential logical structure of IUT may be expressed via ∧ and ∨ (often as XOR ˙∨ if possibilities are disjoint).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives the semantic translation used throughout the exposition that maps boolean operators to geometric/arithmetic operations; underpins the ∧(˙∨)-Chn symbolic summary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 1 (Stp1): log-Kummer-correspondence and Galois evaluation to exhibit Θ-pilot at (0,0)
rubrics_metrics.description: This step consists of exhibiting the Frobenius-like Θ-pilot at lattice point (0,0) of the log-theta-lattice as one possibility within a collection constructed via anabelian algorithms from holomorphic (relative to 0-column) étale-like data; equivalently phrased as negation of non-existence. This step already involves introduction of the (Ind3) indeterminacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies the first concrete algorithmic/logical step in the ∧(˙∨) chain and indicates the role of Ind3 as a coarse algorithmic approximation to the log-Kummer/Galois apparatus.
